description: Building robust applications using Java's object-oriented features. Understanding the usage of Java class libraries. Building multithreaded, platform-independent and GUI based Java applications for business problems.

syllabus.title: Java Fundamentals
syllabus.body: Overview of Java's architecture and the Java Virtual Machine (JVM); classes, objects, basic language elements, primitive data types, variable and method declarations, constructors and constructor overloading, arrays, the main() method and program arguments.

syllabus.title: Packages, Control Flow and Exceptions
syllabus.body: Defining and using packages, scope rules and accessibility modifiers, operators and expressions, control flow statements; exception handling: try, catch, finally, throw, throws, checked and unchecked exceptions.

syllabus.title: Object-Oriented Programming
syllabus.body: Single implementation inheritance, overriding and hiding members, the super reference, chaining constructors; interfaces: definition, abstract methods, polymorphism and dynamic method lookup; fundamental classes: Object, wrapper classes, String, StringBuilder, StringBuffer.

syllabus.title: Multithreading and GUI
syllabus.body: Overview of threads, thread creation, synchronization and thread transitions; basics of event handling and graphics programming using JavaFX.

outcomes: Write Java programs that solve simple business problems.
Create Java applications that are robust and multithreaded.
Write simple GUI interfaces and understand event-based GUI handling principles.
referenceBooks: Y. Daniel Liang, Introduction to Java Programming, Comprehensive Version, Pearson Education, 12th Ed.
Cay S. Horstmann & Gary Cornell, Core Java Volume I, Fundamentals, Sun Microsystems Press, 8th Ed.
